mainTopic: When does a creditor acquire pledged property: retroactively (אביי) or from the due date on (רבא)? Challenges and proofs from רמי בר חמא's case, our משנה about חמץ, and a ברייתא of תנאים
overview: This amud asks when a lender (מלוה) acquires property pledged for a loan. First, the גמרא finishes a case everyone agrees on: if the borrower consecrated the property, the lender redeems it with one extra דינר. The real argument is when the lender himself sold or consecrated it before the due date. אביי says the lender acquires למפרע (retroactively), so his act works. רבא says he acquires only מכאן ולהבא (from the due date on), so it does not. The גמרא challenges רבא from his own advice in a case of רמי בר חמא. There, רבא lets שמעון pay ראובן's orphans with land and then take it back, which seems to require למפרע. It answers that this works for a different reason: רבי נתן's rule that a debtor's debtor pays the original creditor directly. Next, the גמרא tries to prove למפרע from our משנה about a גוי who lent against a Jew's חמץ. It deflects the proof: the חמץ was deposited with the גוי. Finally, it suggests that תנאים argue about this question, but rejects the idea from the end clause of the same ברייתא.

steps.title: Even when the borrower consecrates the property, the lender can redeem it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the agreed case: if the לוה consecrated the pledged property, the מלוה redeems it. It brings a משנה as the source: the lender adds a דינר and redeems the property.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the lender comes and redeems it, as we learned in a משנה: He adds one more דינר and redeems these properties.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a case where everyone agrees: if the borrower consecrated the property, the lender still gets it by redeeming it. It backs this up with a quote from a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The borrower's הקדש cannot wipe out the lender's lien. The lender still has to make a small payment, one extra דינר, to take the property out of הקדש. This is so it does not look like הקדש property is leaving for free. This agreed case sets up the next line, which shows where the real argument lies.

keyTerms.meaning: Redeems (takes property out of הקדש by paying)
As we learned in a משנה
He adds one more דינר (a token payment to הקדש)

phrases.english: and the lender comes and redeems it.
phrases.notes: End of the case where the borrower consecrated the property.

phrases.english: As we learned: he adds one more dinar
and redeems these properties.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the agreed case from the previous text (borrower sold or consecrated) and gives its source.
steps.raayaObject: That a lender can recover property his borrower consecrated by redeeming it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה (ערכין): מוסיף עוד דינר ופודה את הנכסים האלו.

steps.title: The real argument: the lender sold or consecrated it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pinpoints the case of the argument. It is when the lender himself sold or consecrated the property before the loan came due.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they argue is when the lender sold it, or the lender consecrated it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tells us exactly which case אביי and רבא argue about. This line sets up their two opinions, which come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the borrower acted, everyone agrees the lender wins. The question is when the lender acted early, before the due date. Did he already own the property then? That depends on when his ownership begins.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two parties. In the agreed case the borrower (לוה) acted. Here the lender (מלוה) is the one selling or consecrating.

phrases.english: Where they argue
is where the lender sold, or the lender consecrated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts the agreed case with the case under dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute applies only when the lender sold or consecrated the pledged property before the due date.

steps.title: אביי: the lender acquires retroactively
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the lender acquires the property למפרע. Once the borrower fails to pay, it becomes clear the property was the lender's from the start. So his sale or הקדש was valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: He collects retroactively. Since the due date came and the borrower did not pay, it became clear retroactively that from the beginning the property stood in the lender's ownership. So he consecrated properly and sold properly.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives his opinion: the lender's ownership reaches back to the start, so what he did early counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי uses a 'revealed in hindsight' logic (איגלאי מילתא). Failing to pay on time does not create the lender's ownership. It shows the ownership was there all along. That makes the lender's earlier sale or הקדש fully effective.

phrases.english: Abaye said: he collects retroactively.
Since its time arrived and he did not repay it,
the matter is revealed retroactively
that from the outset it stood in his (the lender's) ownership,
so he properly consecrated, and properly sold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first side of the dispute defined in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lender's acquisition is retroactive (למפרע), so his sale or הקדש before the due date is valid.

steps.title: רבא: the lender acquires only from now on
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the lender acquires only מכאן ולהבא. Until the due date, the borrower could have paid cash and freed the property. So the lender only acquires it now, and his earlier sale or הקדש does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: He collects from now onward. Since, had the borrower had money, he would have removed the lender with money, it turns out the lender acquires only now.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא disagrees: the lender becomes owner only when the loan comes due, not before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's logic: right up to the due date, the borrower could pay cash and the lender would get no land. So the lender's ownership cannot reach backward. It starts at the due date. Anything the lender did earlier was done on property he did not yet own.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי says the lender owns it למפרע, so his early sale or הקדש works. רבא says מכאן ולהבא, so it does not, because until the due date the borrower could still pay cash.

phrases.aramaic: וְרָבָא אָמַר, מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא הוּא גּוֹבֶה:
phrases.english: And Rava said: he collects from now onward.
Since if he (the borrower) had money,
he would remove them (pay them off) with money,
it turns out that only now does he acquire.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר, מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא הוּא גּוֹבֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing side to אביי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lender acquires only from the due date onward (מכאן ולהבא), so his earlier sale or הקדש is invalid.

steps.title: Did רבא really say this? The case of רמי בר חמא begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רבא holds מכאן ולהבא. It starts citing a case from רמי בר חמא. ראובן sold a field to שמעון with a guarantee, and the price became a loan. ראובן died, ראובן's creditor seized the field, and שמעון paid the creditor off with money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבא really say this? But didn't רמי בר חמא say: ראובן sold a field to שמעון with a guarantee, and they set the price up as a loan against him. ראובן died. ראובן's creditor came and seized the field from שמעון. Then שמעון came and appeased him with money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a challenge against רבא and lays out the background of a case. The punch line of the challenge has not come yet. This step is the setup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'ומי אמר רבא הכי' signal that רבא may contradict himself elsewhere. The case: שמעון bought a field with a guarantee (אחריות) but never paid. The price became a debt. ראובן's earlier creditor then seized the field, which was mortgaged to him. שמעון kept it by paying the creditor cash.

keyTerms.meaning: Did רבא really say this? (opens a contradiction)
With a guarantee (seller compensates if the field is seized)
Set up the purchase price as a loan owed by the buyer

steps.confusionAlert: Do not look for the contradiction yet. This step only builds the scenario. Step 8 shows how it conflicts with רבא.

phrases.english: And did Rava say this?
But didn't Rami bar Chama say:
Reuven, who sold a field to Shimon with a guarantee,
and set it (the price) upon him as a loan,
and Reuven died,
and a creditor of Reuven came
and seized it from Shimon,
and Shimon came and appeased him with money,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's position from step 4 by citing a related case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that the creditor acquires only מכאן ולהבא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the case of רמי בר חמא, רבא rules that שמעון may pay the orphans with land and then take it back from them (step 7). That only works if the land counts as the father's property, which assumes collection is לְמַפְרֵעַ. Step 8 spells this out.

steps.title: The ruling: ראובן's orphans can demand payment from שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The ruling inside רמי בר חמא's case: ראובן's sons can tell שמעון that the money he owes their father is inherited movables (מטלטלין). Orphans' movables are not liable to a creditor. So שמעון must pay them and cannot offset his loss under the guarantee.
steps.simpleTranslation: By law, ראובן's sons can come and say to שמעון: Our father left movable property with you, and orphans' movables are not mortgaged to a creditor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the legal ruling in the cited case: the orphans win, and שמעון still owes them the price. The challenge to רבא builds on this ruling and is completed in steps 7 and 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמעון is now a creditor of ראובן because of the guarantee. But the money he owes ראובן counts as מטלטלין, and under the rule of that time an orphan's inherited movables could not be collected by their father's creditors. So שמעון cannot simply keep that money as repayment. He has to pay the orphans.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that orphans' movables are not liable to their father's creditor is a basic principle of debt collection. Here it shows that שמעון's debt to ראובן is treated as money, not land. That point matters for the coming question of when a creditor's collection takes effect.

phrases.english: By law, Reuven's sons may come
and say to Shimon:
As for us, our father left movable property with you,

phrases.aramaic: וּמִטַּלְטְלֵי דְיַתְמֵי לְבַעַל חוֹב לָא מִשְׁתַּעְבְּדִי.
phrases.english: and orphans' movables are not mortgaged to a creditor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling for the scenario set up in step 5, as part of the ongoing challenge to רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ראובן's orphans may collect the purchase price from שמעון, because what he owes them is inherited movables, and orphans' movables are not liable to their father's creditor.

steps.title: רבא's advice: שמעון should pay with land and take it back
steps.stepSummary: רבא says a clever שמעון pays the orphans with land and then collects it back from them. He bases this on רב נחמן's rule that land orphans collect for their father's debt can be taken by their father's creditor.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: If שמעון is clever, he pays them with land, and then he collects it back from them. As רב נחמן said: If orphans collected land for a debt owed to their father, a creditor can come back and collect it from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבא's own ruling about the case of רמי בר חמא. This sets up the coming challenge against רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cash the orphans inherit counts as מטלטלין, and a creditor cannot collect from that. But land they inherit can be collected. So שמעון should pay his debt with land. Then, as the creditor under ראובן's guarantee, he takes the same land back from the orphans.

keyTerms.meaning: Orphans, here the heirs of ראובן

steps.whyThisMatters: This is רבא's own statement. The גמרא is about to show that it seems to require לְמַפְרֵעַ, which רבא rejects.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
If Shimon is clever
he pays them with land,
and then he collects it back from them.
As Rav Nachman said:
Orphans who collected land for a debt owed to their father

phrases.aramaic: בַּעַל חוֹב חוֹזֵר וְגוֹבֶה אוֹתָהּ מֵהֶן.
phrases.english: a creditor can come back and collect it from them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the case from רמי בר חמא with רבא's practical advice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמעון should pay the orphans with land, and then he may take it back, because land orphans collect for their father's debt is open to the father's creditor.

steps.title: רבא's advice only seems to work if collection is retroactive
steps.stepSummary: If collection is לְמַפְרֵעַ, the land counts as collected in the father's lifetime, so it can be taken back. If it is מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא, the land is like something the orphans bought, and a creditor cannot collect that. So רבא contradicts himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, if you say a creditor collects לְמַפְרֵעַ, that is why שמעון can take the land back from them. It is as if they collected it while their father was alive. But if you say he collects מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא, why can he take it back from them? It is as if the orphans bought property. And if orphans buy property, is it liable to their father's creditor?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now states the challenge in full. רבא's advice to שמעון seems to fit only the view of אביי (לְמַפְרֵעַ), not רבא's own view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A creditor can only collect from property that was the father's. Under לְמַפְרֵעַ, the land counts as the father's from back when he was alive. Under מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא, the orphans only got it now, after his death, like a new purchase, and a purchase by orphans is not liable for the father's debts.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, if you say (this fits fine)

phrases.english: Granted, if you say
"he collects retroactively,"

phrases.aramaic: אַמְּטוּ לְהָכִי חוֹזֵר וְגוֹבֶה אוֹתָהּ מֵהֶן
phrases.english: that is why he can come back and collect it from them
because it is as if they collected it during their father's lifetime.
But if you say
"he collects from now onward,"
why can he come back and collect it from them?

phrases.aramaic: הָא הָוֵי כְּמַאן דִּזְבֵין יַתְמֵי נִכְסֵי דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: It is as if the orphans bought property,
and if orphans buy property,
is it liable to their father's creditor?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַפְרֵעַ הוּא גּוֹבֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבא's advice from step 7 to attack רבא's view from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that a creditor acquires only מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא lets שמעון reclaim land from the orphans. That only works if the land counts as the father's, which requires לְמַפְרֵעַ. Under מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא, it is the orphans' own purchase, which a creditor cannot take.

steps.title: That case is different because of רבי נתן's rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמעון can claim the land for a different reason. He was bound to the father, and so he is also bound directly to the father's creditor, based on רבי נתן. This has nothing to do with לְמַפְרֵעַ.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because שמעון says to them: Just as I am bound to pay your father, I am also bound to pay your father's creditor. This is based on רבי נתן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא. It says the case of שמעון works for a separate reason that fits even with מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי נתן's rule, a debt owed to the father is really owed straight to the father's own creditor. Here, that creditor is שמעון himself, because of ראובן's guarantee. So the land never truly becomes the orphans' own, and there is no need to say collection works לְמַפְרֵעַ.

keyTerms.meaning: Based on רבי נתן's rule (a debtor's debtor pays the original creditor directly)

steps.confusionAlert: Here the "father's creditor" is שמעון himself. He was owed by ראובן because of the guarantee on the field.

phrases.english: It is different there,
because he says to them:
Just as I am bound to your father,
I am also bound to your father's creditor
based on the rule of Rabbi Nasan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 by giving another reason for רבא's ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (a different legal mechanism)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's advice can only be explained by לְמַפְרֵעַ.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא's advice rests on רבי נתן's direct-debt rule. It fits even with מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא.

steps.title: רבי נתן's source from the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא of רבי נתן: if A is owed by B, and B is owed by C, we take from C and give to A. The source is the פסוק ״וְנָתַן לַאֲשֶׁר אָשַׁם לוֹ״.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי נתן says, From where do we know that if one man is owed a מנה by his friend, and that friend is owed by another friend, we take from this one and give to that one? The פסוק says: "And he shall give to the one he is guilty toward."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רבי נתן's rule, which it used in the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says to pay the one who is truly owed. It does not say to pay whoever you owe on paper. So the last debtor can pay the first creditor directly and skip the middleman. This is what lets שמעון's debt to the orphans go straight to himself.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
One who is owed money by his friend
A sum of one hundred זוז

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge against רבא is answered. Reclaiming land from the orphans works because of רבי נתן's direct debt, not because collection is לְמַפְרֵעַ.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita,
Rabbi Nasan says:
From where do we know that if one is owed a maneh by his friend
and that friend is owed by his friend,
that we take from this one and give to that one?
The verse states:
"And he shall give it to the one he is guilty toward."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the rule used in the answer of step 9.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי נתן, based on the פסוק ״וְנָתַן לַאֲשֶׁר אָשַׁם לוֹ״

steps.title: Proof attempt from the משנה about a גוי's loan on חמץ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if a גוי lent money to a Jew against his חמץ, the חמץ may be used after פסח. This fits well if collection is לְמַפְרֵעַ. The argument continues next.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: If a גוי lent money to a Jew against his חמץ, after פסח the חמץ is permitted for benefit. Granted, if you say the creditor collects לְמַפְרֵעַ, that is why it is permitted for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new attempt to decide between לְמַפְרֵעַ and מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא, using our משנה. This step only sets up the first half of the proof. The challenge to the other view comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under לְמַפְרֵעַ, the חמץ counts as the גוי's from the start of the loan, before פסח. So it was never a Jew's חמץ during פסח, and it is not forbidden afterward. The גמרא is preparing to ask how this works under מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא.

keyTerms.meaning: Lent money with the חמץ as security
Because of this, for this reason

steps.whyThisMatters: This links the money-law debate to איסור חמץ. Whose חמץ it was during פסח decides whether it is forbidden afterward.

phrases.english: We learned in the Mishnah:

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹי שֶׁהִלְוָה אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל חֲמֵצוֹ
phrases.english: A non-Jew who lent money to a Jew against his chametz
after Pesach, it is permitted for benefit.
Granted, if you say
"he collects retroactively,"
that is why it is permitted for benefit.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: גּוֹי שֶׁהִלְוָה אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל חֲמֵצוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the רמי בר חמא challenge was answered, the גמרא starts a new proof from our משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The view that a creditor collects לְמַפְרֵעַ (and a challenge to מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: a גוי who lent against a Jew's חמץ may use it after פסח

steps.title: The other side of the proof: the from-now-on view cannot explain the משנה
steps.stepSummary: If collection works only מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא, the חמץ belonged to the Jew during פסח, so the משנה should not permit benefit from it afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say the creditor collects only from now on, why is the חמץ permitted for benefit? It was owned by the Jew during פסח!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof it started in Step 11. It shows that the view of מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא runs into trouble with the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the from-now-on view, the גוי gets the חמץ only after the Jew fails to pay. That means the חמץ stayed in the Jew's ownership throughout פסח. חמץ that a Jew owned over פסח is forbidden even for benefit. So the משנה's permission seems to prove that collection is לְמַפְרֵעַ.

keyTerms.meaning: Benefit or use (for example, selling it or feeding it to animals)
In the possession or ownership of a Jew
Was standing (here: was located or remained)

phrases.english: But if you say
"he collects from now on,"
why is it permitted for benefit?
It was in the possession of a Jew!
phrases.notes: It was a Jew's חמץ over פסח, so it should be forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא הוּא גּוֹבֶה אַמַּאי מוּתָּר בַּהֲנָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided proof begun in Step 11: the retroactive view fits the משנה well, and the from-now-on view does not.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה permitting benefit after פסח from a Jew's חמץ that was given as security to a גוי lender.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that collection is מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that view the חמץ stayed the Jew's over פסח, so it should be forbidden. The משנה permits it.

steps.title: The case is where the חמץ was deposited with the גוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off the proof: the משנה speaks about a case where the Jew handed the חמץ over to the גוי to keep.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Where he deposited the חמץ with the גוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from Step 12. It explains that the משנה is about a specific situation, not every loan against חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the חמץ physically sat in the גוי's hands during פסח. Because of that, it is treated as the גוי's during פסח, as long as he ends up keeping it. So the משנה can be explained even under מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא, and it no longer proves that collection is retroactive.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (a formula that narrows a source to a specific situation)
He gave it as a deposit or pledge (a security held by the lender)

phrases.english: What are we dealing with here?
When he deposited it with him.
phrases.notes: The חמץ was handed over to the גוי and kept in his possession.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Steps 11–12 by limiting the משנה to a narrow case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the משנה that collection is לְמַפְרֵעַ.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed a general case. The משנה may be about חמץ physically held by the גוי, which works even under מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא.
steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the משנה fails because the משנה can be set in a case where the חמץ was already in the גוי's hands during פסח.

steps.title: Suggestion that תנאים argue about this question
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records an argument between the תנא קמא and רבי מאיר about a Jew who lent to a גוי against the גוי's חמץ. The גמרא suggests that they argue about לְמַפְרֵעַ versus מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is an argument between תנאים? A Jew who lent money to a גוי against the גוי's חמץ does not transgress after פסח. In the name of רבי מאיר they said he does transgress. Isn't this what they argue about: one holds collection is retroactive, and one holds it is from now on?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new idea. It suggests that the same question about how collection works is already an argument between earlier Sages (תנאים).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the Jew is the lender and the גוי's חמץ is his security. רבי מאיר says the Jew transgresses, meaning the חמץ counts as the Jew's over פסח. The suggestion is that he holds collection is לְמַפְרֵעַ, so the Jew owned it already during פסח. The תנא קמא would then hold מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא, so the Jew did not own it during פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say it is like (an argument of) תנאים?
He transgresses (the חמץ counts as owned by a Jew over פסח, so it becomes forbidden)
Is it not that...? (introduces a suggested explanation)

phrases.english: Shall we say it is like a dispute of תנאים:
A Jew who lent to a גוי against his (the גוי's) חמץ —
after פסח he does not transgress.
In the name of רבי מאיר they said: he transgresses.
Is it not that they argue about this:
that one Sage holds he collects retroactively,
phrases.notes: רבי מאיר: so the Jew owned it during פסח.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא הוּא גּוֹבֶה?
phrases.english: and one Sage holds he collects from now on?
phrases.notes: תנא קמא: so the Jew did not own it during פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the משנה is pushed off, the גמרא looks for the same question in an argument between תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: That whether collection is לְמַפְרֵעַ or מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא is an argument between תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא with the argument between the תנא קמא and רבי מאיר about a Jew who lent to a גוי against חמץ.
steps.confusionAlert: Watch who the lender is. Here the Jew is the lender and the חמץ belongs to the גוי. In the משנה from before, it was the reverse.

steps.title: The second half of the ברייתא disproves that explanation
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's next clause says that when a גוי lends to a Jew against the Jew's חמץ, everyone agrees he transgresses. But under the suggested explanation, each Sage should flip his ruling in the reverse case, so they should disagree there too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think that? Read the end of the ברייתא: but a גוי who lent to a Jew against the Jew's חמץ, after פסח everyone agrees he transgresses. They should have said the opposite! The one who said 'he does not transgress' in the first case should say here 'he transgresses.' The one who said 'he transgresses' in the first case should say here 'he does not transgress'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from Step 14. It uses the last part of the same ברייתא to show that the suggested explanation does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the reverse case the גוי is the lender. If collection is retroactive, the חמץ already belonged to the גוי during פסח, so the Jew should not transgress. If collection is from now on, the Jew still owned it during פסח, so he should transgress. So each Sage should flip his ruling. Since the ברייתא says everyone agrees, their argument cannot be about לְמַפְרֵעַ versus מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you really think that? (introduces a rejection)
Read the end (the next clause) of the source
It should have said the opposite

phrases.english: And can you really think that?
Read the end clause:

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל גּוֹי שֶׁהִלְוָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל עַל חֲמֵצוֹ —
phrases.english: But a גוי who lent to a Jew against his (the Jew's) חמץ —
after פסח, everyone agrees he transgresses.
But it should have said the reverse:
for the one who said there "he does not transgress" —
phrases.notes: That's the תנא קמא, who, according to this suggestion, holds מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא.

phrases.english: here he transgresses.
for the one who said there "he transgresses" —
phrases.notes: That's רבי מאיר, who, according to this suggestion, holds לְמַפְרֵעַ.

phrases.english: here he does not transgress!
phrases.notes: If collection is retroactive, the חמץ was the גוי's during פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 14's explanation of the argument between the תנאים.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the תנא קמא and רבי מאיר argue about לְמַפְרֵעַ versus מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That explanation predicts the two Sages would disagree in reverse in the end clause. The ברייתא says everyone agrees there.
steps.whatToRemember: The suggested explanation fails because each side would have to rule the opposite way in the reverse case. The ברייתא says everyone agrees there, so the argument must be about something else.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא technique: test a proposed reason by checking whether it fits every clause of the same source.
